clue.text: To economise, Frenchman is introduced to bonus shares

indicators.note: the Frenchman is brought into the shares, so his letter goes inside them

parts.note: scrip is the name for shares issued free to existing shareholders
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French title for a man

explanation.surface: A thrifty Frenchman is told about the bonus shares his company is handing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be sparing with money, a verb synonym for saving where you can.

clue.text: Place to rest when on a flight

definitions.text: Place to rest when on a flight

parts.words: Place to rest when on a flight
parts.note: a flight here is a flight of steps, not an aeroplane journey; one of its steps is somewhere you can pause

explanation.surface: Where can you take a break while travelling on a plane?
explanation.definitionFit: A single step within a staircase is a spot to pause while climbing, and a staircase is called a flight.

definitions.meaning: in the navy the ordinary sailors, the crew below officer rank, are called by this name
the audience figures measuring how many people watched a television programme

explanation.surface: A television crew pores over the viewing figures for their show.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval usage calls enlisted sailors by this term, while broadcasters use the same word for audience measurement figures.

clue.text: Horse carries mother and boy in preserve

indicators.note: the horse bears the mother and boy within it, so their letters sit inside the horse's

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
ma is an informal word for mother
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A horse bears a mother and her son along with jars of jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, and a preserve is any fruit conserve kept in jars.

clue.text: Priest gets clear compound in gift-wrap

indicators.note: to compound is to mix or combine, so the letters of the word clear are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman is handed a clear chemical compound wrapped up as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something is to wrap it up as a package, which is what gift-wrapping does.

parts.note: RN stands for Registered Nurse

explanation.surface: A business is seeking a nurse to join its staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically an acorn is the nut, and so the fruit, of the oak tree.

definitions.note: the answer is a part of a church rather than a whole one

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance

explanation.surface: A gap has been found inside a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir, so it is a part of the building.

clue.text: Seafood is good to throw out, in a way

indicators.note: the good and the throwing out are placed in the way, inside its letters

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road
to oust is to throw out or expel

explanation.surface: Someone decides seafood is best discarded, in some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, a crustacean eaten as seafood, especially in French cooking.

clue.text: Light lunch initially before the service

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word lunch

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, familiar from words like antenatal
RN is the Royal Navy, known in Britain as the Senior Service

explanation.surface: Someone has a light lunch before attending a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a protective case, so it is a source of light.

clue.text: Gold deposited in leading English bank

indicators.note: the gold is placed inside the word for leading, as one deposits something in a vault

parts.note: main means chief or leading
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold has been lodged with a major English bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' reads as a financial institution, matching 'deposited', but it is a ridge of earth and rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraine is a ridge or mound of debris left by a glacier, a bank of rubble.

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad; the 's joins it to the speech that follows
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Bill gives a speech declaring his love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a poster or advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, a noun synonym for love.

clue.text: Possibly die in Roman instrument of torture

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of die in Roman might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Roman torture device might be where someone could meet their death.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a spiked, coffin-shaped cabinet said to have been used to torture victims, so it is a device of torment.

parts.note: a log is a section of tree trunk

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether to pack a trunk or a hamper for college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'hamper' both look like luggage; hamper is in fact a verb meaning obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog is to block or obstruct, and to hamper is likewise to impede progress.

parts.note: something finished is over, past
A means one; the 's joins it to the food that follows

explanation.surface: Someone has finished their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple food made from wheat dough, a type of food.

clue.text: Cop in real mess in China

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so the letters of cop in real are jumbled

explanation.surface: A police officer finds himself in serious trouble in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C on 'China' suggests the country; it is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine ceramic ware, commonly called china after the country it came from.

clue.text: Take stock — ship is free of corrosion

parts.note: to rustle is to steal livestock, a pun on stock as cattle
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A shipowner assesses the vessel and finds no rust on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' suggests reviewing a situation; here it means stealing cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without rust has escaped corrosion of its iron, so it is free of that decay.

indicators.note: the soldier is placed in the division, his letters inside its letters

parts.note: a section is a division or part
RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier of that corps

explanation.surface: A soldier is dismissed from his army division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests dismissal from the army; it is a bodily fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretion is something released by a gland or organ, a discharge of fluid.

indicators.note: the ridicule and people go in the newspaper, inside its two letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
to rag is to tease or ridicule
men are people

explanation.surface: A newspaper article pokes fun at certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a broken-off part, a synonym for a piece or scrap.

parts.note: an ambler is someone who walks at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A German says that walking is better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective; it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places bets is a better, so a gambler is the same thing.

parts.note: cops is an informal word for the police
E stands for electromotive force in physics, an unusual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A police force searches a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, a small wood.

clue.text: Plain tart takes in Romeo's look

indicators.note: the tart absorbs the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a tart is a pastry, a pie
Romeo is the radio code word for R
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A plain-looking woman catches Romeo's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland, a plain, especially in North America.

parts.note: the steering apparatus of a boat, whimsically said to be built from the word hardwood split as H, the pencil grade for hard, and a familiar timber tree

explanation.surface: Is a ship's steering made of hardwood?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: 'hardwood' splits as H (hard, as on pencils) plus ELM (a wood), which spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiller or wheel by which a ship is steered is known by this name.

clue.text: Oddballs, about to take a beating, stand together

indicators.note: the oddballs go about, around, the beating

parts.note: cranks are eccentric people, oddballs
to lose is to be beaten

explanation.surface: A group of eccentrics, facing a defeat, rally around each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To close ranks is an idiom for uniting in mutual support, as soldiers draw their lines tight.

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of the word cost is used

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: At first, renting a place cost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past tense of rend, split.
explanation.definitionFit: Clove is a past tense of cleave, to split apart, so it means torn or split.

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word for requirement is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a requirement is a need

explanation.surface: Someone has a strong need for a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work dough or muscles with the hands, which is to massage.

indicators.note: everyone is put in the favour, its letters inside

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A unanimous vote in favour gets the cheerful reaction 'That's swell!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as an exclamation of delight but is a verb, to expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell up or inflate rapidly, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: the runs pass through the articles, so their letter goes inside them

parts.note: pieces are items or articles
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone stabs through objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the letter for runs going through the word for articles is itself an act of running something through.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something through is to pierce it, as with a sword.

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of Severn are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A disaster on the River Severn causes anxiety; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge or anxious is commonly described in the plural as a case of this, a synonym for tension.

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of tinned are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that food was tinned wrongly, calling it a nasty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as an adjective, nasty; it is a verb, to have in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to have it in mind as a plan, synonymous with planning.
